answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may influence a decision, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm coordinated duplicate accounts or provable fraud. A single actor can still create many identities, but each must lock real value and risks losing it; splitting influence therefore multiplies the attacker’s capital at risk rather than making votes free. A zenith reputation may earn trust, while quartz records and a whisper-channel audit help expose linked behavior.
